    AI Overview
    A 2026 class-action lawsuit filed against Costco alleges the retailer violates California's Automatic Renewal Law (ARL) by sending membership renewal notices 60 days in advance, rather than the legally required 15 to 45-day window. The suit claims this prevented customers from easily canceling, seeking damages and a jury trial. 
    Key Details of the Lawsuit (Russell George v. Costco): 
    • The Issue: The suit, filed by California resident Russell George, argues that sending notice 60 days before charging the card is too early and fails to give consumers proper notice to cancel.
    • Legal Violations: The complaint alleges violations of California's ARL, False Advertising Law, Unfair Competition Law, and Consumers Legal Remedies Act
      .
    • Impact: The lawsuit claims the early notice resulted in automatic charges of
      for renewals the user did not want.
    • Current Status: Filed in early April 2026, the case seeks class-action status, with a preliminary hearing slated for June 2026. 
    This lawsuit comes amid increased scrutiny on subscription services and "click-to-cancel" requirements for businesses.
